title: Manoj Bajpayee Says OTT Gives Sidelined Actors Respect and a Living
excerpt: In an IANS interview as his Netflix thriller Gajab Raat premieres, Bajpayee says streaming gives actors mainstream cinema could not absorb the roles, respect and stability they were denied.
body:
• Manoj Bajpayee told IANS that streaming platforms have given actors overlooked by mainstream Bollywood substantial roles, public respect and a steady livelihood.
  • "Male actors could not even get consumed by mainstream cinema. They are getting so much respect on OTT," he said in the exclusive interview published October 28.
  • Bajpayee spoke as his latest film, the Netflix suspense thriller Gajab Raat, premiered on October 23, with him playing a police officer opposite Divya Dutta.
  • His own streaming breakthrough, The Family Man, remains the reference point for character-led Indian OTT drama.

Streaming has done what mainstream Bollywood would not: given a generation of overlooked actors real roles, public respect and a way to earn a living. That is the assessment of Manoj Bajpayee, who told IANS in an exclusive interview that performers sidelined by big-screen cinema are now finding substantial work on OTT platforms, New Kerala reported.

"Look at the actors who could not even get rightly consumed earlier. Male actors could not even get consumed by mainstream cinema. They are getting so much respect on OTT."

https://youtube.com/watch?v=BwFuJbHNE4o — Manoj Bajpayee, actor, speaking to IANS

Bajpayee was concrete about what that respect means in practice. "And their lifestyle is maintained. They are finding some kind of comfort in their life because of all those roles that they have been getting," he said. On the pace of the shift, he added: "As a keen observer of the situation, I would say that with OTT, things have been very, very frequent," according to Nation Press's account of the interview.

A Career That Proves the Point

Bajpayee's own filmography maps the divide he describes. His reputation was built on performances mainstream cinema struggled to house at scale — Bhikhu Mhatre in Satya, Sardar Khan in Gangs of Wasseypur and Professor Ramchandra Siras in Aligarh. On streaming, his portrayal of intelligence officer Srikant Tiwari in The Family Man reached a mass audience and became a landmark for long-form, character-driven Indian storytelling. The argument carries weight because it comes from an actor who has worked both systems at the highest level.

https://x.com/Globalstats_77/status/2115807088815305029

The Occasion: Gajab Raat on Netflix

The comments came as Bajpayee's newest release reached viewers. Gajab Raat, a suspense thriller co-starring Divya Dutta in which he plays a police officer, premiered on Netflix on October 23, 2026. The film is produced by Neeraj Pandey and directed by Ritesh Shah. It is the latest in a long line of Bajpayee police roles that includes Shool, Special 26, Traffic, Satyameva Jayate, Dial 100 and Inspector Zende — now arriving via streaming rather than the box office.

Why Diaspora Audiences Feel This Shift

For Indian audiences abroad, streaming is the primary window into new Indian acting talent: the character actors Bajpayee is describing reach living rooms in New Jersey and London on the same day they reach Mumbai. The theatrical-versus-streaming argument is usually framed around budgets and screens. Bajpayee reframes it around people — the performers for whom OTT is not a distribution channel but a livelihood.

What to Watch Next

The test of Bajpayee's claim is in the casting of the next slate of Indian originals: whether the actors streaming rescued keep getting lead and co-lead roles as platforms chase bigger star vehicles, or whether the door he describes starts to close again.
